A lot of prior work addressed key-value (KV) cache selection and compression by sparse attention to enable long-context inference for transformer language models without excessive hardware budgets. We provide a new method for fine-tuning models with sparse attention. It works for any KV cache policy, runs on a moderate hardware budget (e.g., a single Nvidia A100 GPU with 40 GB RAM), and allows the model to co-adapt with the policy, often outperforming models trained with exact attention (sequence parallelism). We also provide an efficient implementation of H2O sparse attention (the leading policy in our experiments) with dedicated scaled dot product attention kernel support. KeysAndValues (https://github.com/awslabs/keys_values), a new open source library for long-context inference and fine-tuning, provides easy-to-use and performant code for all methods discussed here.

(source: arXiv:2509.21845v1, A Comprehensive Evaluation of Transformer-Based Question Answering Models and RAG-Enhanced Design)
sources.arxiv-2502-01113-claim: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has proven effective in integrating knowledge into large language models (LLMs). (source: arXiv:2502.01113v3, GFM-RAG: Graph Foundation Model for Retrieval Augmented Generation)
sources.arxiv-2501-04425-claim: This work introduces systematic approach for enhancing large language models (LLMs) to address Bangla AI mathematical challenges. (source: arXiv:2501.04425v1, End-to-End Bangla AI for Solving Math Olympiad Problem Benchmark: Leveraging Large Language Model Using Integrated Approach)
sources.arxiv-2408-08535-claim: Despite advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, their effectiveness is often hindered by a lack of integration with entity relationships and community structures, limiting their ability to provide contextually rich and accurate information retrieval for fact-checking. (source: arXiv:2408.08535v1, CommunityKG-RAG: Leveraging Community Structures in Knowledge Graphs for Advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Fact-Checking)
sources.arxiv-2607-03953-claim: This study independently replicates and extends the Natural Language Tools (NLT) framework of Johnson et al.~(2025), which questions the use of structured tool calling in large language model (LLM) agentic systems. (source: arXiv:2607.03953v1, The Remarkable Effectiveness of Providing AI Agents with Natural Language Tools: A Replication Study Validating NLT Performance Across 14 Models)
sources.arxiv-2605-28840-claim: Large language model (LLM) agents with tool-calling capabilities are increasingly deployed in production systems, yet a fundamental reliability question remains under-explored: does the same agent behave the same way twice? (source: arXiv:2605.28840v1, How Consistent Are LLM Agents? Measuring Behavioral Reproducibility in Multi-Step Tool-Calling Pipelines)
sources.arxiv-2604-05432-claim: Tool-use large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed to support sensitive workflows, relying on tool calls for retrieval, external API access, and session memory management. (source: arXiv:2604.05432v1, Your LLM Agent Can Leak Your Data: Data Exfiltration via Backdoored Tool Use)
sources.arxiv-2602-21320-claim: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming the foundation for autonomous agents that can use tools to solve complex tasks. (source: arXiv:2602.21320v1, Tool-R0: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Tool-Learning from Zero Data)
sources.arxiv-2606-00135-claim: Tool-calling is a central component of modern large language model (LLM) agents, equipping them with skills beyond their parametric knowledge. (source: arXiv:2606.00135v2, On Effectiveness and Efficiency of Agentic Tool-calling and RL Training)
sources.arxiv-2510-26037-claim: The ability of LLM agents to plan and invoke tools exposes them to new safety risks, making a comprehensive red-teaming system crucial for discovering vulnerabilities and ensuring their safe deployment. (source: arXiv:2510.26037v1, SIRAJ: Diverse and Efficient Red-Teaming for LLM Agents via Distilled Structured Reasoning)
sources.arxiv-2506-01374-claim: While model serving has unlocked unprecedented capabilities, the high cost of serving large-scale models continues to be a significant barrier to widespread accessibility and rapid innovation. (source: arXiv:2506.01374v5, REASONING COMPILER: LLM-Guided Optimizations for Efficient Model Serving)
sources.arxiv-2501-01005-claim: Transformers, driven by attention mechanisms, form the foundation of large language models (LLMs). As these models scale up, efficient GPU attention kernels become essential for high-throughput and low-latency inference. (source: arXiv:2501.01005v2, FlashInfer: Efficient and Customizable Attention Engine for LLM Inference Serving)
sources.arxiv-2408-05499-claim: Recently, there has been an extensive research effort in building efficient large language model (LLM) inference serving systems. (source: arXiv:2408.05499v1, LLMServingSim: A HW/SW Co-Simulation Infrastructure for LLM Inference Serving at Scale)
sources.arxiv-2604-13327-claim: Modern GPU workloads, especially large language model (LLM) inference, suffer from kernel launch overheads and coarse synchronization that limit inter-kernel parallelism. (source: arXiv:2604.13327v2, Event Tensor: A Unified Abstraction for Compiling Dynamic Megakernel)
sources.arxiv-2507-18454-claim: CPUs are critical for LLM serving due to their availability, cost efficiency, and edge applicability. (source: arXiv:2507.18454v2, Sandwich: Joint Configuration Search and Hot-Switching for Efficient CPU LLM Serving)
sources.arxiv-2606-02982-claim: The rapid growth of large language model (LLM) inference services has increased the demand for efficient multi-tenant GPU scheduling. (source: arXiv:2606.02982v2, DriftSched: Adaptive QoS-Aware Scheduling under Runtime Token Drift for Multi-Tenant GPU Inference)
sources.arxiv-1912-02322-claim: Deep learning models are increasingly used for end-user applications, supporting both novel features such as facial recognition, and traditional features, e.g. web search. (source: arXiv:1912.02322v2, Perseus: Characterizing Performance and Cost of Multi-Tenant Serving for CNN Models)
sources.arxiv-2203-09040-claim: Deep Learning (DL) models have achieved superior performance. Meanwhile, computing hardware like NVIDIA GPUs also demonstrated strong computing scaling trends with 2x throughput and memory bandwidth for each generation. (source: arXiv:2203.09040v3, A Survey of Multi-Tenant Deep Learning Inference on GPU)
sources.arxiv-2506-15595-claim: Modern multi-tenant AI clusters are increasingly communication-bound, driven by high-volume and multi-round GPU-to-GPU collective communication. (source: arXiv:2506.15595v5, BandPilot: Toward Performance- and Contention-Aware GPU Dispatching in AI Clusters)
sources.arxiv-1901-05758-claim: With widespread advances in machine learning, a number of large enterprises are beginning to incorporate machine learning models across a number of products. These models are typically trained on shared, multi-tenant GPU clusters. (source: arXiv:1901.05758v2, Analysis of Large-Scale Multi-Tenant GPU Clusters for DNN Training Workloads)
sources.arxiv-2201-03175-claim: Multi-tenant machine learning services have become emerging data-intensive workloads in data centers with heavy usage of GPU resources. (source: arXiv:2201.03175v1, A Simulation Platform for Multi-tenant Machine Learning Services on Thousands of GPUs)
sources.arxiv-2605-21740-claim: LLM agents have incredible potential for scientific discovery applications. However, the performance of LLM agents on real-world, small molecule drug design (SMDD) tasks across diverse chemistries and targets is unclear. (source: arXiv:2605.21740v2, SMDD-Bench: Can LLMs Solve Real-World Small Molecule Drug Design Tasks?)
sources.arxiv-2602-16901-claim: LLM agents are increasingly deployed in long-horizon, complex environments to solve challenging problems, but this expansion exposes them to long-horizon attacks that exploit multi-turn user-agent-environment interactions to achieve objectives infeasible in single-turn settings. (source: arXiv:2602.16901v1, AgentLAB: Benchmarking LLM Agents against Long-Horizon Attacks)
sources.arxiv-2602-03238-claim: LLM agent benchmark scores are shaped not only by the model but also by the agent harness, environment, evaluator, and inference budget. (source: arXiv:2602.03238v3, "LLM Agent Performance" Is Not a Single Evaluation Target)
sources.arxiv-2503-17332-claim: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of autonomously conducting cyberattacks, posing significant threats to existing applications. (source: arXiv:2503.17332v4, CVE-Bench: A Benchmark for AI Agents' Ability to Exploit Real-World Web Application Vulnerabilities)
sources.arxiv-2503-07010-claim: Recently, LLM agents have made rapid progress in improving their programming capabilities. (source: arXiv:2503.07010v2, ProjectEval: A Benchmark for Programming Agents Automated Evaluation on Project-Level Code Generation)
sources.arxiv-2603-22823-claim: Context. The problem of comparative evaluation of communication protocols for task orchestration by large language model (LLM) agents is considered. (source: arXiv:2603.22823v3, Empirical Comparison of Agent Communication Protocols for Task Orchestration)
sources.cache-computing-claim: In computing, a cache is a hardware or software component that stores data so that future requests for that data can be served faster; the data stored in a cache might be the result of an earlier computation or a copy of data stored elsewhere. (source: Wikipedia, Cache (computing))
sources.memoization-claim: In computing, memoization or memoisation is an optimization technique used primarily to speed up computer programs. (source: Wikipedia, Memoization)
sources.trie-claim: In computer science, a trie, also known as a digital tree or prefix tree, is a specialized search tree data structure used to store and retrieve strings from a dictionary or set. Unlike a binary search tree, nodes in a trie do not store their associated key. (source: Wikipedia, Trie)
sources.distributed-computing-claim: Distributed computing is a field of computer science that studies distributed systems, defined as computer systems whose inter-communicating components are located on different networked computers. (source: Wikipedia, Distributed computing)
sources.latency-engineering-claim: Latency, from a general point of view, is a time delay between the cause and the effect of some physical change in the system being observed. (source: Wikipedia, Latency (engineering))
sources.batch-processing-claim: In computing, batch processing is the running of a software job in an automated and unattended way. A user schedules a job to run and then waits for a processing system to run it. (source: Wikipedia, Batch processing)
sources.scheduling-computing-claim: In computing, scheduling is the action of assigning resources to perform tasks. The resources may be processors, network links or expansion cards. The tasks may be threads, processes or data flows. (source: Wikipedia, Scheduling (computing))
sources.network-throughput-claim: Network throughput refers to the rate of message delivery over a communication channel in a communication network, such as Ethernet or packet radio. The data that these messages contain may be delivered over physical or logical links, or through network nodes. (source: Wikipedia, Network throughput)
sources.speculative-execution-claim: In computer science and processor design, speculative execution or speculation is a design characteristic where a processor is able to perform potentially useful work by guessing what work is needed next, compute them prematurely, and immediately applying or discarding the results when the work's necessity is eventually known. (source: Wikipedia, Speculative execution)
sources.branch-predictor-claim: In computer architecture, a branch predictor is a digital circuit that tries to guess which way a branch will go before this is known definitively. The purpose of the branch predictor is to improve the flow in the instruction pipeline. (source: Wikipedia, Branch predictor)
sources.quantization-signal-processing-claim: In mathematics and digital signal processing, quantization is the process of mapping input values from a large set to output values in a (countable) smaller set, often with a finite number of elements. (source: Wikipedia, Quantization (signal processing))
sources.half-precision-floating-point-format-cla: Half precision is a binary floating-point computer number format that occupies 16 bits in computer memory. (source: Wikipedia, Half-precision floating-point format)
sources.attention-machine-learning-claim: In machine learning, attention is a method that determines the importance of each component in a sequence relative to the other components in that sequence. (source: Wikipedia, Attention (machine learning))
sources.transformer-deep-learning-claim: In deep learning, the transformer is a family of artificial neural network architectures based on the multi-head attention mechanism, in which input data such as text, images, or audio, is converted to a sequence of numerical representations called tokens, and each token is converted into a vector via lookup from a word embedding table. (source: Wikipedia, Transformer (deep learning))
sources.mixture-of-experts-claim: Mixture of experts (MoE) is a machine learning technique where multiple expert networks (learners) are used to divide a problem space into homogeneous regions. MoE represents a form of ensemble learning. They were also called committee machines. (source: Wikipedia, Mixture of experts)
sources.sparse-matrix-claim: In numerical analysis and scientific computing, a sparse matrix or sparse array is a matrix in which most of the elements are zero. (source: Wikipedia, Sparse matrix)
sources.information-retrieval-claim: Information retrieval (IR) in computing and information science is the task of identifying and retrieving information system resources that are relevant to an information need. The information need can be specified in the form of a search query. (source: Wikipedia, Information retrieval)
sources.vector-database-claim: A vector database, vector store or vector search engine is a database that stores and retrieves embeddings of data in vector space. (source: Wikipedia, Vector database)
sources.okapi-bm25-claim: In information retrieval, Okapi BM25 is a ranking function used by search engines to estimate the relevance of documents to a given search query. It is based on the probabilistic retrieval framework developed in the 1970s and 1980s by Stephen E. (source: Wikipedia, Okapi BM25)
sources.software-agent-claim: In computer science, a software agent is a computer program that acts for a user or another program in a relationship of agency. (source: Wikipedia, Software agent)
sources.api-claim: An application programming interface (API) is a connection between computers or between computer programs. It is a type of software interface, offering a service to other pieces of software. (source: Wikipedia, API)
sources.compiler-claim: In computing, a compiler is software that translates computer code written in one programming language into another language. (source: Wikipedia, Compiler)
sources.static-program-analysis-claim: In computer science, static program analysis is the analysis of computer programs performed without executing them, in contrast with dynamic program analysis, which is performed on programs during their execution in the integrated environment. (source: Wikipedia, Static program analysis)
sources.intermediate-representation-claim: An intermediate representation (IR) is the data structure or code used internally by a compiler or virtual machine to represent source code. An IR is designed to be conducive to further processing, such as optimization and translation. (source: Wikipedia, Intermediate representation)
sources.multitenancy-claim: Software multitenancy is a software architecture in which a single instance of software runs on a server and serves multiple tenants. Systems designed in such manner are "shared". (source: Wikipedia, Multitenancy)
sources.graphics-processing-unit-claim: A graphics processing unit (GPU) is a specialized electronic circuit designed for digital image processing and to accelerate computer graphics, being present either as a component on a discrete graphics card or embedded on motherboards, mobile phones, personal computers, workstations, and game consoles. (source: Wikipedia, Graphics processing unit)
sources.quality-of-service-claim: Quality of service (QoS) is the description or measurement of the overall performance of a service, such as a telephony or computer network, or a cloud computing service, particularly the performance seen by the users of the network. (source: Wikipedia, Quality of service)
sources.benchmark-computing-claim: In computing, a benchmark is the act of running a computer program, a set of programs, or other operations, in order to assess the relative performance of an object, normally by running a number of standard tests and trials against it. (source: Wikipedia, Benchmark (computing))
sources.reproducibility-claim: Reproducibility, closely related to replicability and repeatability, is a major principle underpinning the scientific method. (source: Wikipedia, Reproducibility)
